title: Redpine Opens 20 Million Research Papers to AI Agents Through Publisher Licensing Deals
key_facts: Swedish company Redpine announced on 6 Oct 2026 that publishers including BMJ Group, Sage, IOP Publishing, IGI Global, Wanfang Data and RCNi joined its content partnerships.
The partnerships span more than 20 million peer-reviewed articles, licensed to AI agents through APIs and the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
Retrieved passages carry identifiers such as DOIs and page references so answers can be traced.
Publishers set permitted uses and pricing; Redpine says it shares the vast majority of revenue with them; the announcement does not say how individual authors are paid.
Sage's participation is a pilot covering more than 400 medical and life-science journals.
Listed pricing is $1 per 1,000 tokens with no upfront subscription.
In a company-published test on 179 expert-validated biomedical questions, an agent with Redpine scored 84.7 against 75.9 for web search alone.
quote_evidence: publishers including BMJ Group, Sage, IOP Publishing, IGI Global Scientific Publishing, Wanfang Data, and RCNi have joined its content partnerships
The announcement does not establish how individual authors will be compensated under their own publishing contracts
They are still vendor-reported findings from a defined benchmark
why_it_matters_hint: Licensed access could let AI answers cite the actual papers, with publishers paid.
notes: Unite.AI's text is itself labelled AI-generated and editor-reviewed; facts come from Redpine's announcement. Benchmark is vendor-run.
